strengths: Novel application of neural solvers to high-speed flows with adaptive time-stepping; addresses an understudied and well-motivated problem
Well-designed two-phase framework with sound technical motivation—correctly identifies why classical CFL cannot be directly applied
Comprehensive ablation studies on neural CFL components and comparison of multiple architectures (U-Net, CNO, F-FNO, Transolver) with different timestep conditioning strategies
Clear presentation with strong physical motivation and thorough appendices; new datasets are released for community use
Reasonable one-step prediction errors (~0.5-2% relative error) and visualizations demonstrate the model captures shock structures and flow dynamics
weaknesses: Critical absence of computational speedup measurements: despite claiming 'great potential for neural acceleration,' the paper provides zero evidence of wall-clock time improvements or FLOPs analysis compared to classical solvers—central claim remains unsubstantiated

Extremely small and homogeneous test sets: only 9-10 held-out cases per problem from the same distribution as training data; no generalization to different Mach numbers, geometries, or initial conditions

Lack of essential baselines: no comparison to uniform time-stepping neural solvers (claimed to be inferior but undemonstrated), no comparison to classical solvers, and no ablation removing the neural CFL component

Limited scope: restricted to 2D simulations at modest resolution (128×128, 104×104) with low Mach numbers (≤2.97, barely supersonic not hypersonic); unclear if approach scales to practical 3D problems

Significant error accumulation over time: correlation time drops to 19-22% for gas velocity y-component in coal dust (Figure 7), indicating narrow reliability window; limited analysis of why different fields have vastly different performance

Test-time distribution shift addressed but not thoroughly validated: paper doesn't analyze whether neural CFL predicts timesteps systematically different from training, or verify stability of predicted sequences

Dataset and generalization concerns: only 90 training cases per problem is small for deep learning; no justification for Mach number ranges; no analysis of whether predictions respect physical constraints (e.g., density positivity)

strengths: Addresses novel and important problem: first systematic treatment of high-speed flows with adaptive time-stepping using neural solvers
Well-designed two-phase framework elegantly separating timestep prediction (neural CFL) from flow evolution, addressing fundamental mismatch between training and inference regimes
Physics-informed design with spatial gradients, max pooling, and CFL features demonstrating solid domain knowledge
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple architectures (U-Net, F-FNO, CNO, Transolver), two diverse datasets (single-phase and multiphase), and multiple metrics
Physically-motivated timestep conditioning strategies inspired by neural ODEs and Mixture of Experts
Strong reproducibility with publicly available code and datasets, detailed hyperparameters and training procedures
Clear presentation with well-articulated motivation and appropriate background on CFD and neural solvers
weaknesses: Critical omission: no wall-clock time comparisons or speedup factors vs. classical solvers, undermining the core claim of 'acceleration' of fluid modeling
Significant error accumulation over long rollouts: unrolled errors reach 5-7% with correlation time proportion degrading to ~60-61%, limiting practical utility
Limited generalization evidence: only 90-100 training cases with 9-10 test cases; no evaluation on unseen parameter regimes, different flow scenarios, or 3D cases
Multiphase results substantially underperform single-phase (coal dust explosion), with volume fraction errors ~18% vs. ~5-6% for other fields, suggesting scalability challenges not addressed
Incomplete baseline comparisons: missing comparisons to simpler adaptive approaches, classical schemes on coarse meshes, and related temporal adaptation methods from recent work
Insufficient analysis of timestep prediction failures: when/why does neural CFL fail? No investigation of stability implications or CFL constraint violations
Validation limited to single CFD solver with no experimental data or comparison to alternative numerical methods
Statistical concerns: very small evaluation sets (9-10 cases) despite tight error bars; sensitivity analyses missing for key design choices (noise level 0.01, coarsening factors, loss functions)
